title: MarkItDown Online - Free Document to Markdown Converter
excerpt: Use MarkItDown Online to convert PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, CSV, JSON, and XML into clean Markdown locally in your browser.
content_html:
Use MarkItDown Online to convert PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON, and XML into clean Markdown.Browser Basic runs locally in your browser; Advanced is for eligible scanned or complex files.

MarkItDown Online is a browser-based document-to-Markdown converter for supported local files. It preserves useful structure such as headings, lists, tables, links, and readable text so the result is easier to review, edit, search, and reuse in ChatGPT, Claude, Obsidian, Notion, and RAG workflows. It is an independent tool and does not provide persistent file hosting, public sharing, or remote downloads.

MarkItDown is an open-source document-to-Markdown converter from Microsoft for LLM and text-analysis workflows.

Choose a supported local file, preview the Markdown, then copy or download the result without installing Python or uploading the source.

Markdown keeps headings, lists, tables, and links easier to reuse in ChatGPT, Claude, Obsidian, Notion, and RAG systems.

MarkItDown AI is independent conversion software, not a file-hosting, file-sharing, cyberlocker, or remote-download service.

Use the web flow when you want one quick Markdown file instead of setting up command-line tools.

Install the original Python package when you need automation, scripting, or controlled processing on your own machine.

Use the browser converter for a quick, supported file that you want to preview and download. Install the original Python package when you need scripts, automation, batch workflows, or format support that this page does not promise.

FeaturesOnline ConverterPython Install
Best forQuick document-to-Markdown conversionDeveloper workflows and automation
SetupOpen the page and choose a fileInstall Python package and dependencies
InputPDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON, XMLDepends on your local package setup
OutputPreview, copy, or download MarkdownMarkdown output for scripts and pipelines
Skill levelNo command line requiredComfortable with terminal commands
Use caseAI notes, docs, knowledge basesBatch jobs, local files, custom tooling

The open-source project can support more formats depending on setup. This online page only promises the formats listed in the local file area.

Choose a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, CSV, JSON, or XML file, or drop it into the local file area.

Wait while the file is converted into Markdown that is easier to inspect, edit, search, and reuse.

Preview the Markdown output, copy it into your workflow, or download it as a .md file.

Conversion focuses on useful document structure rather than pixel-perfect layout. When the source file contains readable text, the result can preserve headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and links in plain Markdown that is easier to inspect and edit.

Section headings create a clear outline for notes, prompts, and RAG chunks. Review the preview when a source uses columns, text boxes, or an unusual reading order.

Bullets, numbered steps, simple tables, and hyperlinks remain easier to reuse than text copied directly from many PDFs or Office files.

Inspect and edit the Markdown, copy it into an AI tool, or download a .md file before adding it to documentation or a knowledge base.

Browser Basic is the default for supported, text-based files and processes them locally in the browser. It does not upload the source file. Advanced is a separate option for eligible scanned or complex documents; it requires sign-in, explains its upload and retention boundary before processing, and may not be available for every account.

Browser Basic does not provide OCR for image-only PDFs. This site also does not fetch remote URLs, host public files, or promise ZIP, batch, audio, or image conversion. If a document contains sensitive information, review the selected mode and on-screen notice before converting.

The original MarkItDown package is designed for developers who want local commands, Python APIs, or controlled automation. For one supported file, the browser converter removes setup; for repeatable or custom workflows, use the package in your own environment.

Best when you just need a quick Markdown file from a supported document.

Best for developers who want the original MarkItDown package in a local or scripted workflow.

Use online conversion for speed, and use the Python package when you need automation or deeper control.

No. This is an independent online converter experience. MarkItDown is an open-source project from Microsoft; this site focuses on making document-to-Markdown conversion easier to use online.

Choose a supported file, preview the Markdown, then copy or download the result.
